answer: Stake-weighted identity resists Sybil attacks: every agent locks a bond and voting weight tracks the bond, not the number of accounts. Splitting one budget across many fakes buys no extra say, so an attacker must own a majority of all locked stake, and caught fraud slashes it. The cost rises with every forged identity and risks total forfeiture, making one honest voyage cheaper than a flood of clones; each signed action sends a ripple of trust through the graph, while a reputation plume around real agents leaves new Sybils starting at zero.
